top10: Evaluation = technical + business + ethical — all gates must pass.
Precision = TP/(TP+FP); Recall = TP/(TP+FN); F1 = harmonic mean.
Accuracy paradox — never trust accuracy on imbalanced data.
Missing is worse → Recall; False alarm is worse → Precision.
Type I = FP; Type II = FN.
Final metrics come from the locked, untouched test set .
Fairness/bias audits are mandatory before deployment.
Validate against Phase I KPIs — lab success ≠ business success.
Deploy / Iterate / Stop — stopping a bad model is good governance.
revision: Phase V = "Good enough?" — technical + business + ethical evaluation.
Use the locked test set for final metrics (first touch!).
Confusion matrix: TP/TN/FP/FN ; Type I = FP, Type II = FN.
Precision = TP/(TP+FP) (predicted); Recall = TP/(TP+FN) (reality); F1 balances both.
Accuracy paradox: imbalanced data → accuracy misleads → use P/R/F1/AUC.
Threshold tradeoff is a business decision (₹ cost of FP vs FN).
Fairness/bias audit + explainability are required gates.
Validate against Phase I business KPIs — technical success alone ≠ success.
Outcomes: Deploy / Iterate / Stop (stop is legitimate!).

examTips.heading: Memory Tricks
bullets: "Cancer & Crime → Recall" (never miss). "Spam → Precision" (never block good mail).
Accuracy + imbalanced data mentioned together = paradox trap → answer uses P/R/F1.
Phase V motto: "Technically good AND business good."

examTips.heading: Keywords
bullets: " Business KPI validation " against Phase I

examTips.heading: Traps
bullets: Choosing accuracy for imbalanced scenarios → wrong.
"Model passed metrics, deploy without business review" → wrong.
"Adjust the model using test results repeatedly" → test set contamination.
Sunk-cost reasoning ("we invested too much to stop") → wrong; stop is valid .
